questions.q: The number of chlorine atoms in $20mL$ of chlorine gas at STP is~_______~${10}^{21}$. (Round off to the Nearest Integer). [Assume chlorine is an ideal gas at STP $R = 0 . 083Lbar{mol}^{- 1}K^{- 1}, {N}_{A} = 6 . 023 \times {10}^{23} ]$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$PV = nRT$

$1 . 0 \times \dfrac{20}{1000} = \dfrac{N}{6 . 023 \times {10}^{23}} \times 0 . 083 \times 273$

$∴$ Number of ${Cl}_{2}$ molecules, $N = 5 . 3 \times {10}^{20}$

Hence, Number of $Cl$ -atoms $= 1 . 06 \times {10}^{21}$

$\approx 1 \times {10}^{21}$

questions.q: A solution of sugar is obtained by mixing $200g$ of its $25 %$ solution and $500g$of its $40 %$solution (both by mass). The mass percentage of the resulting sugar solution is _______ (Nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Mass of solution $= 200 + 500 = 700g$

$25 %$~of sugar solution means~$100g$~solution contain~$25g$~sugar

$40 %$~of sugar solution means~$100g$~solution contain~$40g$~sugar

Mass of sugar $= 0 . 25 \times 200 + 0 . 40 \times 500$

$= 50 + 200 = 250g$

Mass $%$ of resulting solution

$= \dfrac{250}{700} \times 100 = 36 %$

questions.q: $56 . 0L$ of nitrogen gas is mixed with excess of hydrogen gas and it is found that~$20L$ of ammonia gas is produced, The volume of unused nitrogen gas is found to be_____~$L$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: Gay-Lussac's Law proposes a relationship between the combining volumes of gases with respect to the reactants and gaseous products. According to this law, when gases react together to produce gaseous products, the volumes of reactants and products bear a simple whole number ratio with each other, provided volumes are measured at same temperature and pressure.

questions.q: When $0 . 01mol$ of an organic compound containing $60 %$ carbon was burnt completely, $4 . 4g$ of ${CO}_{2}$~was produced. The molar mass of compound is _____~${gmol}^{- 1}$ (Nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Let $M$ is the molar mass of the compound \left(g / mol\right)$
mass of compound $= mole \times molecularmass = 0 . 01Mg$

mass of carbon $= 0 . 01M \times \dfrac{60}{100}$~....(i)

moles of carbon $= \dfrac{massofcompound}{molecularmassofcarbon} = \dfrac{0 . 01M}{12} \times \dfrac{60}{100}$~ ....(ii)

Thus, moles of ${CO}_{2}$~from combustion $= \dfrac{4 . 4}{44} =$0.1 moles of carbon dioxide

Using POAC,
Thus, from (i) and (ii),
$⇒ \dfrac{0 . 01M}{12} \times \dfrac{60}{100} = \dfrac{4 . 4}{44}$

$⇒ M = \dfrac{4 . 4}{44} \times \dfrac{100}{60} \times \dfrac{12}{0 . 01} = 200g / mol$

$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Z is present in least amount so, it will be limiting reagent and amount of product will depend on the amount of Z.

& & & & $X + Y + 3Z \to {XYZ}_{3}initially110 . 05finally1 - \dfrac{0 . 05}{3}1 - \dfrac{0 . 05}{3}\dfrac{0 . 05}{3}$

questions.q: 0.01 mole of an organic compound $(X)$ containing $10 \%$ hydrogen, on complete combustion produced $0.9 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$. Molar mass of $(\mathrm{X})$ is _____ $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Organic compound $\xrightarrow{\text { combustion }} \underset{\substack{\mathrm{0.9} \mathrm{gm}}}{\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}}\therefore$ mole of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}=\frac{0.9}{18}=0.05 \mathrm{~mole}\therefore$ mole of H in $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}=0.05 \times 2=0.1$ mole
= mole of H in 0.01 mole
Organic compound
$\therefore$ wt of H atom in 0.01 mole compound $=0.1 \times 1=0.1 \mathrm{gm}\therefore$ wt of H atom in one mole compound
$=\frac{0.1}{0.01}=10 \mathrm{gm}\because \mathrm{wt} . \%$ of $\mathrm{H}=\frac{\mathrm{wt} \text {. of } \mathrm{H} \text { in one mole compound }}{\text { Molar mass of compound }} \times 1$\begin{aligned}
& 10=\frac{10}{M} \times 100 \\
& \therefore M=100
\end{aligned}$$

questions.q: $10.30$ mg of ${O}_{2}$ is dissolved into a liter of sea water of density $1.03g / mL$ . The concentration of ${O}_{2}$ in ppm is _____________.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Formula of& $p$ pm~is-

$ppm = \dfrac{weightofsolute}{weightofsolution} \times {10}^{6}$

$ppm = \dfrac{10.3 \times {10}^{- 3}}{1030} \times {10}^{6}$ =10

PPM is a concentration term and its full form is "parts per million" and it also can be expressed as milligrams per liter (mg/L). This measurement is the mass of a chemical or contaminate per unit volume of water.

Given that, $1$ mole of $PbS$ is oxidised by $X$ moles of ${O}_{3}$ to get $Y$ moles of ${O}_{2} .$

The balanced chemical equation can be written as,

$PbS + 4{O}_{3} \to {PbSO}_{4} + 4{O}_{2}$

Here $x = 4, y = 4$

Hence,

$X + Y = 4 + 4 = 8$

questions.q: On complete combustion, $0 . 492g$ of an organic compound gave $0 . 792g$ of ${CO}_{2}$. The $%$ of carbon in the organic compound is (Nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$44$~grams of~${CO}_{2}$~contain~$12$~grams of carbon.

Hence, one gram of~carbon dioxide contain~$\dfrac{12}{44}$~gram of carbon.

$0 . 792$~gram of carbon dioxide contain~$\dfrac{12}{44} \times 0 . 792$~gram of carbon

Percentage of carbon =~$\dfrac{Mass of carbon}{Mass of organic compound} \times 100$

$= \dfrac{12}{44} \times \dfrac{0 . 792}{0 . 492} \times 100$

$= 43 . 90 %$

So, answer is~$44$.
